channel.title: The Daily Digest
channel.description: One top story from each of my chosen publications, updated daily.

item.title: NYT: ‘Pretend That I Am Running’: 7 Takeaways From the G.O.P. Midterm Convention
item.description: At a first-of-its-kind midterm convention, President Trump mostly offered retreads and self-congratulation. Then, he offered to pay Americans $5,000 apiece if Republicans kept power.

item.title: NPR: Trump promises Americans $5K if GOP wins. And, Kirk supporters reflect on his death
item.description: President Trump tries to incentivize voters by promising $5,000 to Americans if the GOP wins the midterms. And, young conservatives reflect on the party one year after Charlie Kirk's death.

item.title: BBC News: England's mayors to get power to impose tourist tax
item.description: Hospitality leaders warn the uncapped levy would risk jobs and push prices up for families holidaying in England.

item.title: The Guardian: Twenty-five years after 9/11, the daughter of a hero remembers the mother she lost
item.description: Anna Sweeney Rossman was 5 when her mother, flight attendant Amy Sweeney, was killed aboard American Airlines flight 11 after helping authorities identify the hijackers Anna Sweeney Rossman was only five years old when h…

item.title: Al Jazeera: French Football Federation withdraws support for FIFA President Infantino
item.description: FFF aligns position with of other European federations, such as Belgium, England, Italy, Scotland, and Sweden.

WIRED Backchannel: Excerpt: Emily St. John Mandel’s ‘Exit Party’ Imagines a Future Where a Spy Could Disappear
item.description: In Emily St. John Mandel’s new novel Exit Party, becoming a “ghost” means running afoul of the state. In this excerpt, a secret agent discovers it doesn’t take much.

item.title: WIRED Science: A Satellite Falling Out of Orbit Embarks on Its Final Mission
item.description: Before reentering our atmosphere, the telescopes onboard NASA’s Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory have been restarted to take their last observations.

item.title: WIRED Business: The AI Researcher Who Just Quit Anthropic Says It’s ‘Crunch Time for Humanity’
item.description: Jacob Coxon talks to WIRED about the “mini Manhattan project” inside Anthropic, the problem with alignment, and why AI labs have just a few years left to make their systems safe.

item.title: The New Yorker: Is the Democratic Party Still Too Woke?
item.description: The political operative Adam Jentleson once believed “the way for Democrats to win was to get your base really riled up.” He’s now trying to wrest the Party away from its far-left flank.

item.title: New York Mag The Cut: Do You Want to Buy Princess Diana’s Revenge Dress?
item.description: The iconic look is going up for auction in December.

item.title: New York Mag Curbed: When Offices Don’t Want Their Furniture, She Brings It to NYCHA Residents
item.description: With her rented U-Haul and a small crew, Regina Carter takes what’s destined for the landfill to pop-up giveaways all over the city.
